pathway.title: Encompass Health Corp — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Encompass Health carries USD 2,599.1 million of total debt at carrying value at 30 September 2026, equal to 1.88x trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,379.0 million, or 1.83x net of USD 76.2 million of cash; these are analyst figures on carrying values and company-defined EBITDA, not the covenant ratios, and the covenant maximum is 4.50x [CP-1 Chart data: leverage; Covenants] (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios).

The issuer has USD 947.2 million of liquidity: USD 76.2 million of cash plus about USD 871 million available under a USD 1,000 million revolver that matures on 9 March 2031. Its first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 4.50% notes due 2028, followed by USD 800 million face of 4.75% notes due 2030 [CP-1 Liquidity; Debt by instrument; Chart data: debt maturities] (Documentary Fact).

Revenue is set mainly by government payors. Medicare was 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue, 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and the 2027 Medicare rate update of about 2.3% sits against guided labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% [CP-1A Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact for the mix and update, Management Language for the guidance).

The issuer funds a large capital programme and rising shareholder returns from operating cash flow and debt. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capex of USD 617.2 million, partner distributions of USD 141.8 million, dividends of USD 57.9 million and buybacks of USD 203.7 million left negative USD 62.9 million, and carrying debt rose USD 108.3 million [CP-1 Cash flow quality; CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation] (Documentary Fact for the components, Analyst Interpretation for the net). A correction recorded in the business pack means a Q3 2026 buyback of USD 57.9 million is supplied, which the financial base had listed as not supplied.

The 2026 refinancing pushed half of the 2028 notes out to 2034 at a higher coupon: the weighted coupon on senior notes rose to 4.99% from 4.63%, and the revolver maturity moved from October 2027 to March 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues; CP-1 Debt by instrument] (Analyst Interpretation for the coupon, Documentary Fact for the dates).

Review Choice Demonstration will apply to 108 of the issuer's hospitals from 1 January 2027, and bad debt reserves reached 2.7% of Q3 2026 revenue from 1.9%, attributed by management to a billing disruption after a system conversion [CP-1A Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact; the cause is Management Language). Pre-claim review delays or denies payment, so these two items bear directly on cash conversion.

Interest cover is high: Adjusted EBITDA covered interest excluding amortization 11.7x on a trailing basis at Q3 2026 against a 3.0x covenant minimum [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover] (Analyst Interpretation); cash paid for interest in FY2025 gave 9.5x on the annual report figure, so the basis matters.

cells.text: Provider of inpatient rehabilitation hospital services; 177 hospitals at 30 Sep 2026, of which 110 wholly owned and 67 joint ventures (ownership 50.0% to 97.5%)
Single reportable segment, so no business diversification offsets reimbursement shocks.
"nation's largest owner and operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in terms of patients treated, revenues, and number of hospitals"
Scale claim is the company's own; not independently verified here.
"Substantially all (92%) of the patients we serve are admitted from acute-care hospitals following physician referrals"
Referral dependence on acute-care systems makes joint ventures with those systems a volume protection but also a source of partner claims on earnings.
Hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico with concentrations in Florida and Texas; licensed beds at 31 Dec 2025 were 1,718 in Florida and 1,992 in Texas of 11,465 total
Florida and Texas together hold about a third of licensed beds (see Calculations), so state-level payment, weather or certificate-of-need changes have above-average effect.
Q3 2026: Medicare 66.3%, Medicare Advantage 15.7%, managed care 10.8%, Medicaid 3.1%, other income 2.4%; nine months 2026 Medicare 65.7%
Revenue is set mainly by federal rate updates and Medicare Advantage contracts; a rule change reprices most of the book at once.

CMS 2027 Final IRF Rule: net market basket update of 2.3% effective for discharges from 1 Oct 2026; the company expects a net increase of about 2.3% in Medicare rates. Guidance assumes managed care pricing up 3.5% to 4.0% and salaries and benefits per FTE up 3.5% to 4.0%
10-Q Q3 page:30, page:31; deck Q3 page:7
Expected Medicare price growth below expected labor cost growth per FTE compresses margin unless volume and productivity offset it.
Q3 2026 discharges 69,605 against 65,839, up 5.7%; new-store growth 2.7% and same-store growth 3.0%; occupancy 77.0% against 76.2%; licensed beds 11,722
Growth is split between capacity additions and same-store demand; occupancy near 77% leaves headroom in existing beds.
Salaries and benefits 52.2% of Q3 2026 revenue against 53.1%; contract labor FTEs 272 against 354
Labor is the dominant cost; falling contract labor supported margin in Q3 2026.

Nine months 2026 capex of about $617 million; 2026 guidance about $920 million to $995 million of which about $225 million to $240 million is nondiscretionary; about $535 million additional cost to complete over two years
Growth spending is largely discretionary, giving the issuer a lever to cut cash use in a downturn.
17 IRF development projects announced and underway; 4 hospitals opened year to date with 189 beds
New hospitals carry pre-opening and ramp-up losses that dilute near-term cash flow.

Accounts receivable 712.0 at 30 Sep 2026 against 619.2 at 31 Dec 2025; revenue reserves for bad debt 2.7% of Q3 2026 revenue against 1.9%, "primarily attributable to a billing and collecting disruption issue following a system conversion in Q2 2026"
Documentary Fact; cause is Management Language
Slower collection or higher write-offs convert directly into weaker cash conversion; duration of the disruption is not disclosed.
Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests 53.7 in Q3 2026; distributions paid to them 141.8 for nine months 2026; the company manages its eight consolidated variable interest entities
10-Q Q3 page:7, page:14; deck Q3 page:14
Partner distributions are a recurring cash outflow from the consolidated group.
Owned "approximately 79% of our hospital real estate" at 31 Dec 2025; 103 of 173 hospitals on owned building and land
Owned real estate supports secured borrowing capacity, but about 68% of property held by the company and its guarantors was already pledged to credit agreement lenders at 31 Dec 2025 (10-K page:196).

Review Choice Demonstration extended to Texas (2 Mar 2026), California (1 May 2026) and announced on 25 Sep 2026 for all IRFs billing to one MAC from 1 Jan 2027, covering 108 of the company's IRFs, about 63% of its IRF Medicare claims
Pre-claim review delays or denies payment; affirmation rate thresholds of 80%, 85% and 90% govern opt-out.
Decreased 10.0 in Q3 2026 against Q3 2025 and are reported in Other revenue
Other revenue fell 19.5% in Q3 2026; this is a small but policy-dependent line.

runs.text: Strengths. The issuer has modest leverage, with total debt at 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, and wide room under the 4.50x covenant maximum (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Chart data: leverage). It has ample liquidity of USD 947.2 million and no revolver expiry until March 2031 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Liquidity). Its notes carry fixed coupons, with the first bond maturity in 2028 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Debt by instrument). Demand is nondiscretionary, with 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 67 of 177 hospitals are joint ventures that tie the issuer to referring systems (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Growth capex is largely discretionary, since only about USD 225 million to USD 240 million of 2026 capex is nondiscretionary against a total of about USD 920 million to USD 995 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model), which gives the issuer a lever to protect cash in a downturn. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 346.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 300.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Financials and credit metrics).

Weaknesses. The issuer depends on one payor class for most revenue, with Medicare and Medicare Advantage at 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so a single rule change reprices most of the book (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Review Choice Demonstration coverage will reach 108 hospitals from 1 January 2027 and bad debt reserves are higher, which together put cash conversion at risk (Documentary Fact). Cash flow after growth capex and distributions was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026, so debt rose while leverage stayed modest (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Cash flow quality). Adjusted EBITDA deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests while debt is consolidated in full, and only part of the group guarantees the notes, with the parent and guarantors producing USD 3,016.4 million of the USD 4,793.5 million nine-month 2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Perimeter and Findings). Florida and Texas hold 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 December 2025 (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1A Calculations). Ownership, control rights, covenant ratios, guarantor list and ratings are not evidenced (Insufficient Information, CP-0 Gaps), and missing evidence is not read as an adverse conclusion.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or restructuring in the sources, so the transaction fact pack is a record of 2026 financing and capital events, all executed and all disclosed in the Q3 10-Q (Documentary Fact). On 9 March 2026 the company signed the 2026 Credit Agreement with Truist Bank as administrative and collateral agent, replacing the 2022 agreement that had Barclays as agent. Terms are described as substantially the same except a maturity of 9 March 2031, an undrawn fee lowered by five basis points, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, removal of a 0.10% adjustment on Term SOFR borrowings and a swingline sublimit raised from $25 million to $40 million; a $250.0 million revolver draw repaid the 2022 agreement in full (10-Q Q3 page:18). The agreement is secured by personal property of the company and its subsidiary guarantors. The agreement itself is not in the pack, so the relaxation of restricted payment and debt limits cannot be sized.

In May 2026 the company issued $500 million of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 at par for about $491 million of net proceeds, redeemed $400 million of the $800 million 4.50% Senior Notes due 2028 at par and repaid $100 million of revolver borrowings, recording a $3.2 million loss on early extinguishment in Q2 2026. In August 2026 it issued a further $100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% for about $97 million of net proceeds, used with cash to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:19). The liquidity effect is that revolver drawings fell to 75.0 at 30 September 2026 and availability rose to about $871 million, while total debt at carrying value rose by 108.3 over nine months 2026 (CP-1 reference; deck Q3 page:8). The coupon effect is that the weighted coupon on senior notes rises to 4.99% from 4.63% (Analyst Interpretation, see Calculations): the remaining 2028 notes at $400 million face are callable at par, and the 2034 notes are callable beginning June 2029 per the deck chart (deck Q3 page:11). The use of proceeds to retire lower-coupon debt rather than to fund distributions shows a refinancing motive, though total debt rose in the same period that dividends and buybacks rose.

Other 2026 events: a $17.9 million sale of the 50% equity interest in Gamma Knife Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital agreed on 31 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, with a $17.5 million pre-tax gain in Other income (10-Q Q3 page:12); and a $21.9 million collection in February 2026 from defendants in litigation against former executive officers of the home health and hospice business spun off on 1 July 2022, producing a $16.3 million after-tax gain in discontinued operations (10-Q Q3 page:14). Both are non-recurring and are excluded or separately shown in management's adjusted measures. Subsequent events after 30 September 2026 and before the cutoff are: a dividend of $0.21 per share declared on 22 October 2026 for payment on 15 January 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:43); the Bangor, Maine and San Antonio, Texas hospitals opened in October 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:28); and raised 2026 guidance on 28 October 2026 (deck Q3 page:7). No new debt issue after 30 September 2026 appears in the sources. Ratings and pricing of the new notes against comparables cannot be assessed because no rating or quote is supplied.

fields.value: The financial base is adequate for a consolidated credit snapshot. Reported figures reconcile: operating expense lines sum to the printed totals, the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation returns to pre-tax income, and the debt table ties to the balance sheet and to the maturity table. Encompass Health is a low-leverage, cash-generative issuer on the evidence supplied: total debt to trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA is 1.88x at Q3 2026, net debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 1.83x, EBITDA to interest excluding amortization is 11.7x, and revolver availability is about $871m. The 2026 refinancing moved the revolver maturity from October 2027 to March 2031 and replaced $400m of the 2028 notes with 2034 notes, so no bond matures before the remaining $400m of 2028 notes. Three points temper the view. First, the company deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests inside Adjusted EBITDA while reporting debt on a fully consolidated basis, and only part of the group guarantees the notes. Second, free cash flow after capex, noncontrolling distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative for nine months 2026, so debt rose while revenue and EBITDA grew. Third, the covenants are stated as compliance only, and the agreements that define them are not in the pack. The leverage and coverage figures below are therefore analyst calculations on carrying values and reported Adjusted EBITDA, and are not the covenant ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health is the largest owner and operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals on its own description, with 177 hospitals in 39 states and Puerto Rico at 30 September 2026, 67 of them joint ventures. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor, acquisition or restructuring in the pack: the transactions in the period are financings, a small equity-method disposal, a litigation recovery and shareholder distributions. The business is a single segment whose revenue is set largely by government reimbursement, so the creditor risk mechanics run through Medicare rate updates, claim review and denial rules, labor cost inflation and the pace of capacity additions, rather than through sponsor behaviour. The sources show a company that has funded growth with operating cash flow and the revolver while raising dividends and buybacks, and that refinanced half of its 2028 notes into 2034 notes at a higher coupon. Credit-relevant strengths are the nondiscretionary patient base, referral dependence on acute-care hospitals that is also a joint-venture channel, and long-dated fixed-rate debt. Credit-relevant weaknesses are payor concentration, regulatory review expansion from 2027, a billing disruption that lifted bad debt reserves in Q3 2026, geographic concentration in Florida and Texas and a growth plan that consumes more cash than operations generate after distributions. Ownership, control rights and sponsor alignment cannot be assessed beyond the public-company facts, because the proxy statement is not in the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no sponsor transaction, acquisition or restructuring in the sources, so the transaction fact pack is a record of 2026 financing and capital events, all executed and all disclosed in the Q3 10-Q (Documentary Fact). On 9 March 2026 the company signed the 2026 Credit Agreement with Truist Bank as administrative and collateral agent, replacing the 2022 agreement that had Barclays as agent. Terms are described as substantially the same except a maturity of 9 March 2031, an undrawn fee lowered by five basis points, relaxed limits on investments, debt, liens and restricted payments, removal of a 0.10% adjustment on Term SOFR borrowings and a swingline sublimit raised from $25 million to $40 million; a $250.0 million revolver draw repaid the 2022 agreement in full (10-Q Q3 page:18). The agreement is secured by personal property of the company and its subsidiary guarantors. The agreement itself is not in the pack, so the relaxation of restricted payment and debt limits cannot be sized.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In May 2026 the company issued $500 million of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 at par for about $491 million of net proceeds, redeemed $400 million of the $800 million 4.50% Senior Notes due 2028 at par and repaid $100 million of revolver borrowings, recording a $3.2 million loss on early extinguishment in Q2 2026. In August 2026 it issued a further $100 million of the 2034 notes at 98.75% for about $97 million of net proceeds, used with cash to repay revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:19). The liquidity effect is that revolver drawings fell to 75.0 at 30 September 2026 and availability rose to about $871 million, while total debt at carrying value rose by 108.3 over nine months 2026 (CP-1 reference; deck Q3 page:8). The coupon effect is that the weighted coupon on senior notes rises to 4.99% from 4.63% (Analyst Interpretation, see Calculations): the remaining 2028 notes at $400 million face are callable at par, and the 2034 notes are callable beginning June 2029 per the deck chart (deck Q3 page:11). The use of proceeds to retire lower-coupon debt rather than to fund distributions shows a refinancing motive, though total debt rose in the same period that dividends and buybacks rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other 2026 events: a $17.9 million sale of the 50% equity interest in Gamma Knife Center at Barnes-Jewish Hospital agreed on 31 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, with a $17.5 million pre-tax gain in Other income (10-Q Q3 page:12); and a $21.9 million collection in February 2026 from defendants in litigation against former executive officers of the home health and hospice business spun off on 1 July 2022, producing a $16.3 million after-tax gain in discontinued operations (10-Q Q3 page:14). Both are non-recurring and are excluded or separately shown in management's adjusted measures. Subsequent events after 30 September 2026 and before the cutoff are: a dividend of $0.21 per share declared on 22 October 2026 for payment on 15 January 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:43); the Bangor, Maine and San Antonio, Texas hospitals opened in October 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:28); and raised 2026 guidance on 28 October 2026 (deck Q3 page:7). No new debt issue after 30 September 2026 appears in the sources. Ratings and pricing of the new notes against comparables cannot be assessed because no rating or quote is supplied.

fields.value: Overall behaviour reading: Neutral or Mixed. Evidence quality: High for issuer filings and decks as primary dated sources for the facts above, and Insufficient for ownership and control because the proxy statement is absent. No score is stated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: Medicare 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue and 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals (10-Q Q3 page:33; 10-K page:9). Mechanic: nondiscretionary demand supports volume, but nearly all price-setting is administrative, so a rule change reprices most revenue at once and referral channels depend on acute-care partners. Implication: revenue visibility is high on volume and low on rate; debt service capacity depends on regulatory outcomes more than on competition. Counter-evidence: the pack contains no logged conflict against this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Medicare rate update of about 2.3% against assumed labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% (10-Q Q3 page:31; deck Q3 page:7); bad debt reserves up to 2.7% of revenue from 1.9% (deck Q3 page:5); review expansion to 108 hospitals from 1 Jan 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:31). Mechanic: a price-cost gap and slower collections reduce EBITDA and cash conversion together. Implication: leverage of 1.88x leaves cushion, but a combined margin and collection shock would reduce the cash available for growth capex and distributions first. The conflicting account-receivable figures logged below limit how precisely cash conversion can be traced.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Concentration risk. Evidence: Florida and Texas beds of 3,710 out of 11,465 and a single segment (10-K page:110, page:216). Mechanic: state-level events hit a third of capacity. Implication: modest diversification within a single reimbursement system.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Sponsor alignment. Not applicable as a sponsor concept: the company is listed with no named sponsor. Alignment is with public shareholders through dividends and buybacks, which were partly debt-funded in nine months 2026. Implication: monitor distribution pace against free cash flow after growth capex.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health Corp is a moderately leveraged, cash-generative inpatient rehabilitation operator whose credit is sound but exposed to government reimbursement. Its strongest support is financial: total debt was 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, liquidity was USD 947.2 million, and the first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 2028 notes. Its weakest point is that Medicare and Medicare Advantage supplied 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so price updates and claim-review rules can move earnings quickly, while cash flow after capex, partner distributions, dividends and buybacks was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026. The outcome depends on whether review expansion from 1 January 2027 and the billing disruption erode cash conversion before the issuer slows growth capex or shareholder returns.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Encompass Health carries USD 2,599.1 million of total debt at carrying value at 30 September 2026, equal to 1.88x trailing four quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,379.0 million, or 1.83x net of USD 76.2 million of cash; these are analyst figures on carrying values and company-defined EBITDA, not the covenant ratios, and the covenant maximum is 4.50x [CP-1 Chart data: leverage; Covenants] (Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the ratios).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer has USD 947.2 million of liquidity: USD 76.2 million of cash plus about USD 871 million available under a USD 1,000 million revolver that matures on 9 March 2031. Its first bond maturity is USD 400 million face of 4.50% notes due 2028, followed by USD 800 million face of 4.75% notes due 2030 [CP-1 Liquidity; Debt by instrument; Chart data: debt maturities] (Documentary Fact).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is set mainly by government payors. Medicare was 66.3% and Medicare Advantage 15.7% of Q3 2026 revenue, 92% of patients are admitted from acute-care hospitals, and the 2027 Medicare rate update of about 2.3% sits against guided labor cost growth per FTE of 3.5% to 4.0% [CP-1A Company and operating model] (Documentary Fact for the mix and update, Management Language for the guidance).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer funds a large capital programme and rising shareholder returns from operating cash flow and debt. For nine months 2026, operating cash flow of USD 957.7 million less capex of USD 617.2 million, partner distributions of USD 141.8 million, dividends of USD 57.9 million and buybacks of USD 203.7 million left negative USD 62.9 million, and carrying debt rose USD 108.3 million [CP-1 Cash flow quality; CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation] (Documentary Fact for the components, Analyst Interpretation for the net). A correction recorded in the business pack means a Q3 2026 buyback of USD 57.9 million is supplied, which the financial base had listed as not supplied.

fields.value: The 2026 refinancing pushed half of the 2028 notes out to 2034 at a higher coupon: the weighted coupon on senior notes rose to 4.99% from 4.63%, and the revolver maturity moved from October 2027 to March 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues; CP-1 Debt by instrument] (Analyst Interpretation for the coupon, Documentary Fact for the dates).

Pre-claim review delays or denies payment, so these two items bear directly on cash conversion.

fields.value: Interest cover is high: Adjusted EBITDA covered interest excluding amortization 11.7x on a trailing basis at Q3 2026 against a 3.0x covenant minimum [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover] (Analyst Interpretation); cash paid for interest in FY2025 gave 9.5x on the annual report figure, so the basis matters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The issuer has modest leverage, with total debt at 1.88x trailing Adjusted EBITDA at Q3 2026, and wide room under the 4.50x covenant maximum (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Chart data: leverage). It has ample liquidity of USD 947.2 million and no revolver expiry until March 2031 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Liquidity). Its notes carry fixed coupons, with the first bond maturity in 2028 (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Debt by instrument). Demand is nondiscretionary, with 92% of patients admitted from acute-care hospitals, and 67 of 177 hospitals are joint ventures that tie the issuer to referring systems (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Growth capex is largely discretionary, since only about USD 225 million to USD 240 million of 2026 capex is nondiscretionary against a total of about USD 920 million to USD 995 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model), which gives the issuer a lever to protect cash in a downturn. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 346.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 300.1 million (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Financials and credit metrics).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. The issuer depends on one payor class for most revenue, with Medicare and Medicare Advantage at 82.0% of Q3 2026 revenue, so a single rule change reprices most of the book (Documentary Fact, CP-1A Company and operating model). Review Choice Demonstration coverage will reach 108 hospitals from 1 January 2027 and bad debt reserves are higher, which together put cash conversion at risk (Documentary Fact). Cash flow after growth capex and distributions was negative USD 62.9 million in nine months 2026, so debt rose while leverage stayed modest (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 Cash flow quality). Adjusted EBITDA deducts net income attributable to noncontrolling interests while debt is consolidated in full, and only part of the group guarantees the notes, with the parent and guarantors producing USD 3,016.4 million of the USD 4,793.5 million nine-month 2026 revenue (Documentary Fact, CP-1 Perimeter and Findings). Florida and Texas hold 32.4% of licensed beds at 31 December 2025 (Analyst Interpretation, CP-1A Calculations). Ownership, control rights, covenant ratios, guarantor list and ratings are not evidenced (Insufficient Information, CP-0 Gaps), and missing evidence is not read as an adverse conclusion.
